To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inflammation causes changes of mu-opioid binding and G-proteins coupling in primary sensory neurons.
peripheral inflammation induces a significant increase in mu-opoid receptor binding sites and G-protein activation in dorsal root ganglion of primary sensory neurons.
inflammation causes an increase in MOR binding and an increase in MOR G-protein signaling in primary afferents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the peripheral analgesic actions of opioids.
the effects of inflammation-induced peripheral MOR activation on the analgesic efficacy of peripherally active MOR agonists.
the development of new peripherally restricted opioids with high selectivity, high affinity, high efficacy and high specificity to MOR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peripheral analgesic effect of opioids in inflammation is caused by the up-regulation of the peripheral opioid receptor system.

inflammation causes a significant increase in MOR density and G-protein activation in primary afferents, which may be responsible for the enhanced antinociceptive effect of full and partial MOR agonists.
the inflammatory state increases the sensitivity of peripheral MORs, which in turn may be a major factor contributing to the peripheral analgesic effect of opioids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

inflammation induces an up-regulation of peripheral MORs that is associated with an increase in MOR G-protein signaling, which is most likely caused by a shift from the full to a partial agonist profile.

inflammation-induced changes in MOR binding sites and G-protein-coupling properties of full and partial agonists in DRG neurons are likely to contribute to the peripheral analgesic properties of opioids.
peripheral inflammation induces an increase in MOR density and a sensitization of MOR signaling in primary afferents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
peripheral inflammation induces an increase in the number of MOR and an up-regulation of G-protein coupling.
inflammation-induced changes in MOR G-protein function in DRG neurons can be exploited for developing novel analgesics.

inflammation-induced changes in MOR binding sites and G-protein-coupling efficiency in primary afferents may be a key factor that contributes to the efficacy of peripheral opioids in inflammatory painful states.
